To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the rate of growth of sarcoma-37 is modified during culture, and that this alteration is dependent upon the type of culture medium used.

(1) Sarcoma-37 cells grown in contact with chick embryos for 10 days or more have a growth rate that is significantly slower than that of cells grown for a shorter period or in vitro; (2) this growth-rate modification is reversible, since cells that have been cultured for a long time can be returned to their former growth rate by a short exposure to fresh medium, and (3) this growth-rate effect is not due to a change in the nutritional requirements of the cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effect of (a) culture in vitro, (b) the chick embryo as a culture medium, (c) the chick embryo in the presence of a tumour, (d) the chick embryo with or without tumour in the presence of tumour cells, (e) the chick embryo without tumour in contact with tumour cells, and (f) the chick embryo, without tumour, in contact with tumours.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the growth potential of the tumour cells is altered during culture.
the growth-rate is altered in the following ways : (1) The growth-rate is increased when sarcoma-37 is transferred to the chick embryo.

the growth-rate of sarcoma-37 is modified during culture in the avian embryo, and that the modification is a function of the time during which the tumour is grown in the host, the age of the host at the time of inoculation, the number of tumour cells inoculated and the number of passages through the host.

the tumour cells grown in contact with chick embryo tissue do not show any marked change in the rate of growth.

culture of the tumour cells in contact with the avian host does indeed modify the growth rate of the tumour in the host.
